headline: Manning's arm too much for Clemson in dominant 49-17 Texas rout
body: Arch Manning put on a clinic in the second half, turning what looked like a competitive matchup into a complete dismantling. The Texas quarterback finished 29 of 47 for 409 yards and five touchdowns, finding soft spots in Clemson's coverage all afternoon. What made the performance remarkable wasn't just volume—it was efficiency. Manning rarely held the ball longer than needed and made clean decisions under pressure, letting his receivers settle into routes rather than forcing balls into tight windows.

Texas's ground game gave Manning time to operate. Running back Wisner carried the load with 101 yards on nine carries, including two short-yardage scores that took pressure off the passing attack. That balance—101 rushing yards paired with 405 passing—gave the Clemson defense no rhythm to find. Meanwhile, Clemson's quarterback Cortez managed only 247 yards and struggled with timing throughout the day. The Tigers were held to just 49 rushing yards, a sign that their offensive line couldn't establish any foundation.

Clemson's defense couldn't generate sustained pressure despite three opportunities from turnovers. Defensive end Carter logged six tackles and a sack, staying active even as his teammates fell out of sync. But one player's effort wasn't enough against a Texas team that controlled line of scrimmage on both sides. The 32-point margin reflects a complete performance from Texas—field position, execution, and limiting mistakes all aligned at once.
turningPoint: Late in the second quarter, Manning connected with Worthy for a 101-yard reception that broke the game open and forced Clemson into a 32-7 hole entering halftime, essentially deciding the outcome.

unsungHero.name: Biles
unsungHero.why: While Manning rightfully earned Player of the Game honors, Biles's two sacks and three tackles set the tone for Texas's defensive dominance, keeping Clemson's offense off-balance and preventing any rhythm-building drives that might have kept the score respectable.
